# Pinned to non-heir-backoff=1.5 (the v1 default): this file tests v1's
# "non-heirs back off so the heir fires first" ordering. Since
# DESIGN_UPDATE.md D3 the default is 1.0 (stock timers), which only keeps
# the heir first once D1's short heir timeout lands.

# T4.5 (TASKS.md) -- crash-path biased election timeouts, double-failure
# fallback (DESIGN.md §2.5/§3): the leader AND the heir both crash. The
# remaining non-heir followers must still elect eventually via their
# backed-off timeouts -- no deadlock, and the "bounded regression" DESIGN.md
# promises (delayed by at most (NonHeirBackoff-1)*electionTimeout+jitter
# versus vanilla, then proceeds exactly like ordinary Raft). Written first
# per the TDD convention.
#
# 5 voters so a majority (3 of 5) remains reachable without the 2 dead
# nodes. "Dead" means simply never ticked or stabilized again below --
# every stabilize call here is scoped to the 3 survivors only. Only one
# survivor (3) is advanced through ticks; the other two (4, 5) are left
# untouched so they simply grant 3's vote well within their own backed-off
# window -- this keeps the scenario deterministic (a real double-failure
# fallback can also produce a split vote among equally backed-off
# survivors, since none of them is biased to go first, but which one wins a
# three-way race depends on each node's independent random draw, which
# would make a byte-for-byte golden file flaky across runs; the "no
# deadlock, majority still elects" property is what DESIGN.md actually
# requires here, and that's what this demonstrates).
#
# Tick count for node 3 is exactly 2 rounds (2*electionTimeout=6 ticks), not
# an arbitrary "enough" number: the backed-off threshold's range is
# [NonHeirBackoff*electionTimeout, NonHeirBackoff*electionTimeout+electionTimeout-1]
# = [4,6] for electionTimeout=3, so 6 ticks guarantees crossing it (equality
# counts) on every possible draw, while leaving at most 2 ticks accumulated
# toward node 3's *next* (post-campaign, vanilla-range >=3) timeout -- too
# few to ever cross that one too. That makes "exactly one campaign, no
# matter the random draw" a structural guarantee, not a coincidence of this
# particular run -- unlike a looser "just tick it a few extra rounds"
# approach, which free (and did, in an earlier draft of this file) produce a
# second, spurious self-re-election before the vote round was even
# delivered, making the golden file flaky across runs.

log-level error
----
ok

add-nodes 1 voters=(1,2,3,4,5) index=2 heir-election=true stability-score=50 non-heir-backoff=1.5
----
ok

add-nodes 1 voters=(1,2,3,4,5) index=2 heir-election=true stability-score=255 non-heir-backoff=1.5
----
ok

----
ok

add-nodes 1 voters=(1,2,3,4,5) index=2 heir-election=true stability-score=90 non-heir-backoff=1.5
----
ok

add-nodes 1 voters=(1,2,3,4,5) index=2 heir-election=true stability-score=80 non-heir-backoff=1.5
----
ok

# No deadlock: despite losing both the leader and its designated heir, the
# remaining majority (3 of 5) elected a new leader among themselves in a
# single round -- 4 and 5, never advanced past their own (equally backed-off
# but untouched) timeout, simply granted 3's vote. 1 and 2's lines below are
# stale/unreachable -- neither was ever ticked or stabilized past the
# announcement round above.
